A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same R1-Code-Interpreter work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original training curves, benchmark accuracies in Table 3, response analyses and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds OOD evaluations, comparison methods and training ablations.

M1.justification: v3 introduces evaluated online curriculum variants that recompute improvement potential before each stage, with cumulative merging or separate groups (Section 5.3). These are limited procedural adaptations; the principal model, response loop, rewards, SFT initialization and fixed four-stage GRPO method remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluation on GPQA Diamond graduate-level science questions and AIME 2024/2025 mathematics problems (Table 4), substantially extending external evaluation coverage. The original 144 tasks and their capability classifications are retained.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds Qwen3-14B using All Text and CodeSteer. Figure 7 additionally compares GRPO with PPO and Reinforce++, while Figure 8 adds online curriculum alternatives. These broaden the evaluated comparator set beyond v2; the original comparators remain.

E3.justification: The original training settings and 107/37 task split remain. Added protocols include training on 107 SymBench/Reasoning-Gym tasks with BBH withheld and two-stage GRPO (Figure 13), equal-sized improvement-potential groups (Figure 14), online repartitioning and another RL round. New SFT controls vary prompt diversity, multi-turn emphasis and inclusion of 6.5k additional incorrect trajectories.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained framework, warm-start and base-model ablations, v3 tests optimizer dependence, static versus online curricula, merging, continued RL, SFT data design and improvement-potential strata (Figures 7–10 and 14). Figure 13 adds a benchmark-held-out generalization analysis. These directly examine previously untested design choices and failure conditions.

E5.justification: v3 specifies three-run averages for the new OOD results in Table 4 and adds error bars to the retained SFT framework comparison, redrawn as Figure 9a. The error-bar definition and seeds remain unspecified. This documents additional uncertainty reporting without establishing increased runs for earlier results.

E6.justification: All original Table 3 entries are unchanged. Added entries include Qwen3-14B average test scores of 62.4 for All Text and 64.4 for CodeSteer. New Table 4 reports R1-CI-14B scores of 50.2 on GPQA and 42.0 on combined AIME 2024/2025. Added ablations report degradation with incorrect SFT data and no improvement from another RL round; these are new findings, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: The GRPO equations, improvement-potential definition, assumptions, propositions and proofs are retained. The theoretical analysis moves from Appendix C in v2 to Appendix D in v3, with corresponding renumbering rather than substantive mathematical changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, principal contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about general-purpose code interpretation, potential-guided curricula, training efficiency, self-checking and performance against GPT-4o. The new experiments support these claims without redefining their central scope.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations of training choices: online repartitioning offers faster convergence at greater inference cost, another RL round can overfit its initial data group, and incorrect SFT trajectories increase instability. It also argues that prompt diversity and multi-turn emphasis matter and that the framework transfers across RL optimizers. These extend the explanation of applicability and failure conditions.

D1.justification: v3 discloses the four improvement-potential intervals and explicitly identifies the SFT ablation models as 7B. Its new reproducibility statement refers to supplementary training/data-synthesis code and an open-source release after acceptance, while retaining the abstract's existing availability links. These are documentation additions; actual resource availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for PPO, Reinforce++ and GPQA. The substantive related-work discussion, including positioning against ToRL, ReTool and ToolRL, is retained and relocated from Section 6 to Appendix A.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. v3 moves related work to the appendix, reorganizes appendix headings, shortens the multi-turn ablation explanation and adds ethics, reproducibility, writing-assistance and acknowledgment sections. It also corrects Table 2's erroneous '15 agents' heading to '4 agents'; both versions already describe four agents.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 7, 8, 10, 13 and 14, the SFT-design panel in Figure 9b, and OOD Table 4. It consolidates and redraws v2's appendix Figure 9 as main-text Figure 9a and expands Table 3 with Qwen3 rows. This substantially changes the experimental displays, alongside relocation and resizing of retained figures.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens validation of the central claims. External GPQA/AIME evaluations and benchmark-held-out BBH testing address v2's limited evidence beyond its original benchmark sources. Equal-sized potential-group tests and data/curriculum ablations directly support training choices and reveal useful failure conditions, including harmful incorrect SFT data and unproductive additional RL. The original results and theory remain. Undefined error bars and inconsistent release wording limit reporting quality, but the added empirical support provides a clear substantial net improvement.
